text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostToIga(x) ::: x lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x is at Roland Garros 2022.
CocoGauff ::: Coco Gauff.
QuestionPred ::: the statement about Coco Gauff's loss and activity.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly, then they are one of the most active players.
∀x (LostToIga(x) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly.
∀x (FemalePlayer(x) → LostToIga(x)) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x))) ::: All players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros2022(x) → LostToRafaelNadal(x)) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostToRafaelNadal(CocoGauff)) → ¬MalePlayer(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male player.
AtRolandGarros2022(CocoGauff) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
¬(LostToIga(CocoGauff) ∧ ActivePlayer(CocoGauff)) ::: Coco Gauff is not both a player who lost to Iga Świątek and one of the most active players.
